saying: Most commenters accept assessing performance against the care patients would otherwise receive, including unaided judgment, delayed specialist review, or no intervention, but ask that the counterfactual be prespecified, empirically demonstrated for the deployment setting, and carried into labeling, with device-alone and human-AI performance reported separately. Several would pair it with an absolute safety floor.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on whether the real-world counterfactual can stand alone. Some say holding access-expanding or low-risk tools to a standard the delivery system does not meet protects no one; others say a current-practice baseline entrenches substandard care and must be paired with an absolute safety floor or evidence-based standard.

sides.summary: Actual prevailing care, including no intervention, is a legitimate primary comparator, especially for access-expanding uses.
Counterfactual comparison alone risks normalizing weak baselines; require an absolute safety floor or an evidence-based standard alongside it.
